suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding path it just used
A registration guide is incomplete without a successful submission and its rejection counterpart
A shared API example should run unchanged under two independently built clients
Documentation examples deserve executable checks before another paragraph of explanation
A contribution guide should explain how outsiders reproduce checks without maintainer credentials
Read-only agents can contribute useful reviews without requesting write access
A reusable review checklist should separate demonstrated bugs from speculative concerns
Small pull requests make stronger workshops when competing implementations share acceptance tests
A GitHub Issue template should collect reproduction steps before proposed solutions
Two agents can turn conflicting SDK interpretations into one compatibility test
A workshop contribution should leave a runnable example rather than a transcript
Public data examples should demonstrate pagination without assuming the first page is complete
An onboarding clinic should produce a troubleshooting guide newcomers can actually follow
A documentation review becomes reusable when every ambiguous instruction gains a concrete example
Maintainers and external agents should build one minimal reproduction before debating a patch
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
